svg.text: Define your schema once in PostgreSQL. Deploy anywhere with SQLite.

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: #475569; line-height: 1.55; text-align: justify;
xhtml:div.xhtml:p: Your PostgreSQL schema is more than just tables. It encodes data types (UUID, JSONB, TIMESTAMP), constraints (foreign keys, unique, check), PL/pgSQL triggers with arbitrary business logic, Row-Level Security policies that control exactly who can see and modify each row, and powerful extensions like pgvector for AI embeddings, PostGIS for geospatial queries, and tsvector for full-text search.

pg2sqlite ships the hard parts. RLS policies are compiled into views plus INSTEAD OF write triggers. PL/pgSQL bodies are reshaped into SQLite trigger CTE chains. pgvector, PostGIS, and tsvector are routed through sqlite-vec, geolite, and FTS5 with the sync triggers that keep them coherent. Role-based GRANT permissions decide which tables and rows each device receives, and optional sync-time auditing detects rows that should have been invisible under the active RLS policy.

Correctness is held in place by a heavy verification stack: 1,300+ integration tests across 131 files, 43 insta snapshots that lock the verbatim translated SQL, reverse-translation round-trips that check SQLite output reparses to PostgreSQL, and two honggfuzz harnesses (forward and reverse) whose past crashes are pinned as 55 regression fixtures that re-run on every commit.

g.text: Every PostgreSQL type mapped to SQLite
SUM(CASE WHEN c THEN x END)

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #64748b; line-height: 1.55; text-align: justify;

foreignObject.xhtml:div: Not every table needs to be on every device. pg2sqlite reads the PostgreSQL GRANT permissions for your app's database role and decides how to handle each table: skip it entirely, create a read-only copy, or build a fully writable version with Row-Level Security enforcement.

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #64748b; line-height: 1.55;

foreignObject.xhtml:div: In PostgreSQL, Row-Level Security policies control which rows each user can read, insert, update, or delete. pg2sqlite translates these policies into SQLite views and INSTEAD OF triggers, so the same per-user data filtering works on every device without application code changes.

g.text: Text search translated to SQLite FTS5

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #64748b; line-height: 1.55;

foreignObject.xhtml:div: AI-powered apps store embeddings (numeric representations of text, images, or other content) alongside regular data. pg2sqlite translates pgvector columns into sqlite-vec virtual tables with automatic sync triggers, enabling similarity search directly on local devices.

text.tspan: sqlite-vec v0.1.x uses brute-force O(n). ANN indexing planned:

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #64748b; line-height: 1.55;

foreignObject.xhtml:div: PostGIS columns become BLOBs and ST_* calls are dispatched to the geolite SQLite extension. GiST indexes are translated into CreateSpatialIndex calls that build an rtree shadow table with sync triggers. Bbox-narrowable predicates like ST_Intersects are rewritten to route through that rtree, so spatial queries hit a real index instead of a full table scan.

g.text: 9 bbox-narrowable predicates auto-route through the rtree shadow:
ST_Intersects, ST_Contains, ST_Within, ST_Covers, ST_CoveredBy, ST_Equals, ST_Touches, ST_Crosses, ST_Overlaps

xhtml:div.style: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #64748b; line-height: 1.55;
xhtml:div.xhtml:p: In local-first apps, a sync engine writes data directly into the local SQLite database. Some synced rows may belong to other users and should be invisible to the current user according to your Row-Level Security policies. This feature automatically detects those unauthorized rows after sync, records each violation in an audit table, and provides a view to query all problematic rows at any time.
